The 2027 road plan for early career associates and the groups that employ them. Thirteen proposed road rooms sit on top of the published 200-level Spear and CDOCS dates. Dr. Jen Bell's course is the front door. The Growth Accelerators come next, picked doctor by doctor. Click a city to see which groups can fill the room. This is the Growth Prescription on the road. It is not the Early Career Accelerator program, and it is not Spear's full 2027 event plan.

Loading the flight plan

Two different things

A program and a prescription

This flight plan is the Growth Prescription on the road. It sits beside the Early Career Accelerator, which is a separate program. They are built differently. They stay separate for now, and this page keeps them apart.

Growth Prescription

The courses and where they run

Nothing here is a fixed sequence. A group or a doctor is prescribed the courses they need and takes them in the room closest to them.

The path

What comes after the front door

The next step after Dr. Bell's course is a Growth Accelerator, not the core curriculum. Core comes later, for the doctor who wants to keep going.

StartFront door

Dr. Jen Bell. The default start. A group that teaches its own treatment planning can skip it and start at an accelerator.

ThenGrowth Accelerators, first tier

Endo, restorative, and surgery and bone grafting. Any order, and only the ones a doctor needs. The restorative workshop is being reworked.

NextGrowth Accelerators, next tier

Aligners, implants and sleep, for the associate who has the basics down.

AlignersReady to sellOne room proposed, pending Align.
ImplantsReady to sellNo room in this plan yet.
SleepConcept onlyNot built yet.
LaterCore curriculum

For the doctor who wants more. Not every doctor will go on to it, and that is fine.

Proposed format, not on offer yet

How a room could be built

A proposal for 2027, not what is on sale today. The idea is that the two days in the room become the middle of a course, not all of it.

BeforeOnline learning

The concepts, done at home, so the live days go further.

The roomTwo days live

Hands-on for endo, restorative and surgery. Case work for the front door and aligners.

AfterLive roundtable

A follow-up with faculty, so the skills show up in the practice.

Groups have asked for a workshop with an online program and a roundtable attached. Endo is the closest to that today. For every other course the online piece still has to be built or refined.

Proposed, not on offer yet

After the room: making it stick

The live days are where a skill gets learned. The 90 days after are where it shows up in production. The proposal is that every road room comes with an implementation track, so the doctor, the team and the group all leave with a plan.

Day 1A 90-day plan

Each doctor leaves with three cases to do in the next 30 days and targets for 60 and 90 days.

In the front door course
For the officeThe team kit

Scripts, patient education pieces and case presentation templates for the front desk and the treatment coordinator, so the whole office helps the patient say yes, not just the doctor.

To build
MonthlyFaculty follow-up

A live roundtable and case submission, so doctors get feedback on their first real cases.

Closest for endo
For the groupThe group lead's playbook

A one-page guide for the group's clinical director: how to support each doctor after the course, what to watch for, and when to step in.

To build
Day 90The 90-day scorecard

Before and after numbers for each doctor: procedures done in-house against referred out, case acceptance, and production on that course's procedures. This is what shows the group its return.

To build
Any timeOnline library

Spear's online content mapped to each course, so the doctor knows what to watch next.

Content exists, to map

Status: the roundtable is closest for endo today. The scorecard, the team kit and the playbook still need to be built.

Growth Prescription tracks

One front door. A different path for every doctor.

This is the prescription at work: no fixed pathway. A group does not send everyone to everything. Pick a home city and build two tracks. The plan finds the closest room for each step and puts it in date order.

The front door is the top of the funnel and the default start, not a requirement. A group with its own treatment planning program can send doctors straight to the Growth Accelerators, taken in any order, by the doctors who need them. The step after the front door is a Growth Accelerator, not the core curriculum.
